data.title: Over half of Apple users plan to upgrade to iPhone 18: survey
data.description:
Evercore ISI's latest iPhone survey indicates Apple (AAPL) should enjoy a stronger-than-normal upgrade cycle and benefit from higher average selling prices.

"We see not just room for units to do well, but critically, we think pricing could be >20% driven by a combination of ASP increases, higher-priced SKUs, and a shift up in memory configurations," said Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani in a Friday investor report.

"Pricing trends continued to grow, with our survey reflecting an aggregate ASP of $1,374, up nearly 28% and well above our long-term survey average," he said.

The survey found that 53% of the nearly 4,000 consumers taking part plan to buy an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max. This is up from the average of 51%. It also discovered that 32% of respondents intend to buy the Pro Max compared to 29% in last year's survey. Fourteen percent said they will purchase Apple's new product, the iPhone Duo, compared to 9% last year who said they would buy the new iPhone Air. 

"Our 2026 iPhone survey points to a solid upgrade environment, with 61% of respondents planning to purchase an iPhone. This is slightly higher than last year's survey of 59% and marks the second strongest response in our survey's history and well above our survey average of 45%," Daryanani said.

Beyond the iPhone, there was a slight increase in respondents planning to upgrade their Apple Watch and AirPods.

Evercore retained its Outperform rating on Apple and increased its price target to $380 from $365.

data.title: Market's '3 Ps are all peaking' as rotation takes hold - BofA
data.description:
Bank of America Securities is warning investors that the stock market's (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ) primary drivers—positioning, profits and policy—are peaking, signaling a structural market rotation is already underway.

Market positioning is "too bullish," BofA reiterated in its latest Flow Show note, with the Bull & Bear Indicator triggering a 9.5 sell signal again and fund-manager positioning hitting the 100th percentile. Moreover, a record net 33% of fund managers now report companies are overinvesting.

 

Concurrently, profit expectations are moderating into 2027 as "GDP boom hopes are over," while monetary policy has shifted away from a "run it hot" posture, requiring higher bond (TLT) (ZROZ) risk premiums to restore credibility.

The macro shift is actively driving sector rotation. Since the Nasdaq's (QQQ) peak on June 1st, rising Federal Reserve hike expectations have deflated early leaders, specifically AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) enablers like "blue-collar semis" (SMH) (SOXX) and independent power producers, the note said.

 

 

For investors, BofA outlined a specific playbook: while it is "not yet time for defensives," a pivot toward quality (QUAL), value (VFVA), and yield looks prudent. However, the firm cautions that current market winners—commodities, credit and China bonds—represent key vulnerabilities heading into the fourth quarter.

data.title: Revvity slips as CFRA downgrades on limited near-term upside
data.description:
Revvity (RVTY) shares fell on Friday following a five-day winning streak as CFRA downgraded the life sciences company to Hold from Buy, citing a less attractive upside opportunity in the near term after its recent rally. 

“Though we think RVTY’s fundamental story remains compelling, we think near-term upside is less attractive following recent valuation expansion,” analyst Daniel Rich wrote, according to Bloomberg.

The Waltham, Massachusetts-based company, formerly known as PerkinElmer, has added nearly 50% in value this year, with the stock trading near a post-pandemic high. The downgrade came after its shares set a new 52-week high earlier this week after the company presented at Baird’s 2026 Global Healthcare Conference.

“We look to 3Q results to help confirm indications of instrument backlog conversion and software sales momentum, which we think could lead to stronger earnings guidance that helps normalize RVTY’s valuation," Rich added as he boosted his price target to $157 from $145 per share.

data.title: Large and mega-cap financial stocks with the weakest momentum grades
data.description:
Large- and mega-cap financial stocks with the weakest momentum grades have posted significant declines so far this year, with the ten names on the list earning Momentum Grades ranging from F to D-.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Momentum Grade measures a stock's momentum relative to other stocks in its sector. The grade is derived from a comparison of multiple momentum indicators, including medium- and long-term price performance, against sector peers.

Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (FMCC) and Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA) were the only large- and mega-cap financial stocks to receive an F Momentum Grade, with YTD declines of 55.82% and 53.96%, respectively.

The Carlyle Group (CG) and Coinbase Global (COIN) were among the stocks rated D-, falling 31.03% and 24.78%, respectively. Fidelity National Financial (FNF), also with a D- grade, had the smallest decline of 19.73%.

data.title: Former Wells Fargo asset manager Allspring explores $4B sale - FT
data.description:
Allspring Global Investments, the former asset management division of Wells Fargo (WFC), is considering a sale that could value the firm at about $4 billion.

Talks are said to be in the early stages, and no final decision has been made, according to a Financial Times report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Wells Fargo (WFC) sold Allspring to private equity firms GTCR and Reverence Capital in 2021 for $2.1 billion.

GTCR declined to comment to Reuters. Reverence and Allspring did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Wendy’s franchise operator Meritage seeks bankruptcy protection
data.description:
Meritage Hospitality Group (MHGU), one of Wendy’s (WEN) largest U.S. franchisees, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as the restaurant operator seeks to restructure its finances amid weak sales at the burger chain.

The Grand Rapids, Michigan-based company operates 314 Wendy’s (WEN) restaurants across the Midwest and Southeast, as well as one Bojangles location and five Morning Belle restaurants, according to Nation’s Restaurant News.

Meritage (MHGU) listed between $10 million and $50 million in assets and liabilities in its bankruptcy filing and has about $150 million in debt owed to City National Bank, NRN reported.

The filing follows Meritage’s (MHGU) closure of 60 Wendy’s (WEN) restaurants earlier this year as the company moved to reduce costs and improve profitability. It has also stopped or modified breakfast service at underperforming locations, according to the publication.

Meritage (MHGU) said the bankruptcy process would help strengthen its balance sheet and provide greater financial flexibility. The company also plans to seek debtor-in-possession financing to support operations while it restructures.

Wendy’s (WEN) has struggled with declining sales and traffic in the U.S. Same-store sales fell 7% in the second quarter, prompting the company to cut its dividend and withdraw its financial outlook for the year.

Wendy’s (WEN) said it works with franchisees facing financial challenges on a case-by-case basis and remains focused on supporting its franchise system.

Meritage (MHGU) said it remains confident in the potential for a turnaround of the Wendy’s (WEN) brand.

Shares of Wendy (WEN) were trading about 4% lower in the afternoon trade on Friday.

data.title: JPMorgan, Banco Santander lead £1.1B loan for Drax's solar acquisition - report
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Banco Santander (SAN) are leading a group of banks arranging debt financing of more than £1B to fund Drax Group's (DRXGF) (DRXGY)  purchase of Bluefield Solar Income Fund, according to a media report on Friday.

NatWest Group (NWG) is also involved in the financing that put £1.1B ($1.5B) in bridge funding in place for the purchase, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The banks will seek to market the debt to institutional investors later this year or in early 2027, the people said. Drax (DRXGF) (DRXGY) may also look to refinance outstanding debt, they added.

The financing to pay for the renewable energy acquisition comes as lenders are ready to sell more than $138B of buyout debt in coming months, Bloomberg  said, citing JPMorgan estimates.
